title: Guest access: who can your tenant invite, and what can guests reach?
summary: Hold: Microsoft documents a beta API for the domain invitation list and explicitly states the US Government invitation default, so neither is wholly undocumented. The page also overstates how long existing guests retain access and understates the available workforce guest add-ons.

claims.claim: Guest access uses Microsoft Entra B2B collaboration, part of External ID, to share tenant applications and resources with external guests.
claims.quote: Microsoft Entra External ID includes collaboration capabilities that allow your workforce to work securely with business partners and guests.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: Partners use their own identities and credentials whether or not they have a Microsoft Entra account.
claims.quote: The partner uses their own identities and credentials, whether or not they have a Microsoft Entra account.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: After invitation redemption or self-service sign-up, the guest is represented in the directory as a user object.
claims.quote: Once the guest redeems their invitation or completes sign-up, they're represented in your directory as a user object.

claims.quote: The user type for these B2B collaboration users is typically set to "guest"

claims.quote: Cross-tenant access settings control whether users can authenticate with external Microsoft Entra tenants. They apply to both inbound and outbound B2B collaboration.

claims.quote: You allow B2B collaboration with Fabrikam in your cross-tenant access settings, but then you add fabrikam.com to your blocked domains in your external collaboration settings. Your users can't invite new Fabrikam business guests

claims.quote: existing Fabrikam guests can continue using B2B collaboration.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits: Open invitations by default
claims.claim: By default every user, including guests, can invite external users.
claims.quote: By default, all users in your organization, including B2B collaboration guest users, can invite external users to B2B collaboration.
claims.fix: Qualify both default statements: 'By default, everyone, including guests, can invite external users except in US Government, where allowInvitesFrom defaults to none.' The cited collaboration page gives the general default, but https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/resources/authorizationpolicy?view=graph-rest-1.0 states the US Government exception.

claims.claim: Invitations can go to any domain at the documented domain-list default.
claims.quote: By default, the Allow invitations to be sent to any domain (most inclusive) setting is enabled.

claims.claim: External ID billing uses MAU, counting unique external users who authenticate within a calendar month.
claims.quote: The basic External ID billing model is based on monthly active users (MAU), which is the count of unique external users who authenticate to your tenants within a calendar month.

claims.claim: The External ID MAU model applies to all guest users.
claims.quote: The MAU billing model for External ID applies to all guest users.

claims.claim: For B2B collaboration, MAU billing applies only to external users with UserType Guest, not organizational Member users.
claims.quote: For B2B collaboration, the MAU billing model applies only to external users who have a UserType value of Guest. It doesn't apply to users who originate from within the organization and have a UserType value of Member.

claims.claim: The External ID FAQ states that the core offering is free for the first 50,000 MAU.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Entra External ID core offering is free for the first 50,000 MAU.

claims.claim: External ID requires an Azure subscription for billing.
claims.quote: External ID requires an Azure subscription for billing.

claims.claim: A workforce tenant must be linked to an Azure subscription.
claims.quote: Microsoft Entra workforce tenants must be linked to an Azure subscription for proper billing and access to features.

claims.claim: Premium add-on charges are additional to basic MAU billing.
claims.quote: Premium add-on charges are in addition to the basic MAU billing.

claims.claim: Two premium add-ons apply to guests in workforce tenants: ID Governance and GSA for Guests.
claims.quote: | SMS Phone Authentication | Workforce, External | Transaction-based | Additional charges for each SMS-based authentication event
claims.fix: Change 'Two apply to guests in workforce tenants' to 'Two MAU-based add-ons apply to guests in workforce tenants'. This narrows the claim to the two named MAU add-ons without denying the documented transaction-based SMS add-on.

claims.claim: ID Governance is a MAU-based add-on for guests in workforce tenants.
claims.quote: | ID Governance | Workforce | MAU-based | Govern guest users with premium features in Microsoft Entra ID Governance.

claims.claim: GSA for Guests is a MAU-based add-on for workforce tenants.
claims.quote: | GSA for Guests | Workforce | MAU-based | Global Secure Access (GSA) coverage for guest users in workforce tenants. |

claims.where: Risks and limits: Lists are not retroactive; controls[2].note

claims.quote: Changing the default inbound or outbound settings to Block access could block existing business-critical access to apps in your organization or partner organizations.

claims.quote: If a user invitation is in a pending state, and you set a policy that blocks their domain, the user's attempt to redeem the invitation fails.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Cross-tenant access is not an invitation block

claims.quote: Cross-tenant access settings, inbound access does not prevent users from sending invitations, nor prevent them from being redeemed.
claims.fix: Replace the bullet's first sentence with: 'Microsoft's architecture guide says inbound cross-tenant access controls application access and token issuance rather than invitation or redemption, but the configuration guide says cross-tenant settings are checked at invitation and Block access can prevent invitations.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/architecture/5-secure-access-b2b and https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/external-id/cross-tenant-access-settings-b2b-collaboration together to expose the documented disagreement.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Device policies lock guests out

claims.where: Risks and limits: Device policies; What to check: Conditional Access
claims.claim: Device-compliance Conditional Access policies block guests unless they are excluded.

The cited Zero Trust page gives the exclusion advice; https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/external-id/authentication-conditional-access documents device trust as an alternative.

claims.claim: Guest invitation permissions are at Microsoft Entra admin center > Entra ID > External Identities > External collaboration settings > Guest invite settings.
claims.quote: Browse to Entra ID > External Identities > External collaboration settings. Under Guest invite settings, choose the appropriate settings:

claims.claim: PATCH /v1.0/policies/authorizationPolicy sets guest invitation permissions through allowInvitesFrom with the four named values.
claims.quote:
PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/policies/authorizationPolicy
Indicates who can invite external users to the organization. The possible values are: none, adminsAndGuestInviters, adminsGuestInvitersAndAllMembers, everyone.

claims.claim: Guest directory visibility is at Microsoft Entra admin center > Entra ID > External Identities > External collaboration settings > Guest user access.
claims.quote: Browse to Entra ID > External Identities > External collaboration settings. Under Guest user access, choose the level of access you want guest users to have:

claims.claim: PATCH /v1.0/policies/authorizationPolicy sets guest directory access through guestUserRoleId for User, Guest User or Restricted Guest User.
claims.quote:
PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/policies/authorizationPolicy
User (a0b1b346-4d3e-4e8b-98f8-753987be4970), Guest User (10dae51f-b6af-4016-8d66-8c2a99b929b3), and Restricted Guest User (2af84b1e-32c8-42b7-82bc-daa82404023b).

claims.claim: The invitation domain list is at Microsoft Entra admin center > Entra ID > External Identities > External collaboration settings > Collaboration restrictions.
claims.quote: Browse to Entra ID > External Identities > External collaboration settings. Under Collaboration restrictions, select Deny invitations to the specified domains.
claims.fix: The path stops on the right settings page. Complete the block-list route as 'Entra ID > External Identities > External collaboration settings > Collaboration restrictions > Deny invitations to the specified domains > Target domains'; the allow-list option on the same page is 'Allow invitations only to the specified domains (most restrictive)'.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented an API for the B2B invitation domain allow or block list.
claims.quote: Represents Microsoft Entra B2B features in Microsoft Entra External ID for workforce tenants, including restricting/allowing which domains can be used to invite users
claims.fix: Replace null with kind 'graph', call 'PATCH /beta/policies/b2bManagementPolicies/{b2bManagementPolicyId}', and docs 'https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/b2bmanagementpolicy-update?view=graph-rest-beta'. Add to the note: 'The request body updates definition, the JSON-string collection defining the policy. This API is beta, is not supported for production applications, and is available in the global service only.' Keep the narrower v1.0 question.

claims.claim: Default inbound cross-tenant access settings are reached through the printed Cross-tenant access settings > Default settings > Inbound access settings > Edit inbound defaults route.
claims.quote:
Browse to Entra ID > External Identities > Cross-tenant access settings, then select Cross-tenant access settings.
On the Default settings tab, under Inbound access settings, select Edit inbound defaults.
claims.fix: The route reaches the inbound settings pane, not the final B2B control. Complete it as 'Entra ID > External Identities > Cross-tenant access settings > Cross-tenant access settings > Default settings > Inbound access settings > Edit inbound defaults > B2B collaboration > External users and groups > Access status'.

claims.claim: PATCH /v1.0/policies/crossTenantAccessPolicy/default configures default inbound and outbound B2B collaboration access.
claims.quote:
PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/policies/crossTenantAccessPolicy/default
b2bCollaborationInbound
b2bCollaborationOutbound
claims.fix: Keep the call and append to controls[3].note: 'The request body sets b2bCollaborationInbound and b2bCollaborationOutbound.'

claims.claim: Inviting a guest starts at Microsoft Entra admin center > Entra ID > Users > New user > Invite external user.
claims.quote: Browse to Entra ID > Users. Select New user and then Invite external user.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/invitations creates an individual guest invitation.
claims.quote:
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/invitations
invitedUserEmailAddress | string | The email address of the user you're inviting.
claims.fix: Keep the call and append to controls[4].note: 'The request body names the guest through invitedUserEmailAddress; resetRedemption resets an existing guest invitation.'

claims.claim: The printed Microsoft Entra Conditional Access policy route reaches the Guest or external users assignment.
claims.quote:
Browse to Entra ID > Conditional Access > Policies. Select New policy.
Under Assignments, select Users or workload identities.
Under Include, choose Select users and groups, and then select Guest or external users.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/identity/conditionalAccess/policies creates a Conditional Access policy that can target guest or external users.
claims.quote: includeGuestsOrExternalUsers | conditionalAccessGuestsOrExternalUsers | Internal guests or external users included in the policy scope. Optionally populated.
claims.fix: Keep the method and path, which the cited creation reference documents. Append to controls[5].note: 'The request body targets guests through conditions.users.includeGuestsOrExternalUsers.'

claims.claim: Teams guest access is configured at Teams admin center > Users > Guest access > Guest access.

[-AllowGuestUser <Boolean>]
If $true, guests in your tenant will be able to access the Teams client. Note that this setting has a core dependency on Guest Access being enabled in your Office 365 tenant.
